hooks.text: We have been drawing the Sun the wrong color our entire lives.
Why is the yellow Sun actually pure white in space?
The yellow star we see daily is actually a blindingly white beacon.

title: Why the Sun Isn't Actually Yellow
description: The Sun appears yellow from Earth, but it is actually blindingly white. Discover how our atmosphere steals blue light to create this cosmic illusion.

beats.text: We have been drawing the Sun the wrong color our entire lives.
beats.visual: Sun photographed from the International Space Station, 2018

beats.text: For generations, children's drawings and even professional astronomers have classified our star as a yellow dwarf.
beats.visual: Children's drawing of a yellow sun in a blue sky

beats.text: But astronauts aboard the International Space Station observe a brilliant, blindingly white disk set against black space.
beats.visual: Astronaut photograph of the Sun from the International Space Station, 2021

beats.text: Surprisingly, the Sun’s actual peak emission is in the green portion of the visible spectrum.
beats.visual: Diagram comparing the solar spectrum blackbody curve with peak green emission, 2015

beats.text: Human eyes perceive this broad mixture of wavelengths as white because it stimulates all our color receptors simultaneously.
beats.visual: Light refraction through a glass prism showing the rainbow spectrum, 2017

beats.text: This yellow star we see from Earth is actually an atmospheric illusion called Rayleigh scattering.
beats.visual: Portrait of physicist Lord Rayleigh John William Strutt, 1890
queries: Lord Rayleigh John William Strutt portrait

beats.text: Nitrogen and oxygen molecules deflect blue light away, leaving the remaining direct sunlight appearing yellow to our eyes.
beats.visual: Diagram illustrating atmospheric Rayleigh scattering of blue light, 2019

beats.text: This stolen blue light paints our sky, while the leftover rays make us believe our white star is golden.
beats.visual: Beautiful sunset showing Rayleigh scattering and a reddened solar disk, 2022
